agent_answer:
The conversation shows a warm but strained relationship between Kwame and Dev within the group.

- **Kwame** is the one pushing Dev to be more present. He calls Dev out for being “MIA for like six weeks,” tells him he “has to actually come,” and asks him to at least send a voice note or meme. He also makes a personal effort beyond the group: he travels to Edinburgh as a separate trip specifically to see Dev, knowing Dev is heads-down in the archive (“He's heads-down at the moment but I wanted to see him”), and later reassures Dev he missed a good meetup but was “there in spirit.”

- **Dev** is the one repeatedly absent and apologetic. He blames archive/PhD work (“head down in the archive”), says he “genuinely want[s] to come,” and promises things will get easier “when the PhD is done.” He also expresses gratitude toward Kwame for the Edinburgh visit — “Kwame thank you for Edinburgh last week 💙” — showing appreciation for Kwame’s effort.

So the dynamic is one of mutual warmth but persistent friction: Kwame is frustrated by Dev’s absence yet still invests in him personally, while Dev appreciates that investment but keeps failing to follow through on group commitments.
